Iran has bombed Iraq. Saudi Arabia. UAE. Bahrain. Qatar. Kuwait. Jordan. Turkey. Even Cyprus. 16 days of war. Missiles and drones in every direction. But one country right on Iran's border hasn't been touched - Pakistan. And Pakistan has US military reconnaissance operations on its soil. So why is Iran leaving Pakistan alone? This is one of the most interesting strategic questions of this entire war. And the answer reveals something much bigger than just Pakistan. First — let's establish what we know as fact. Pakistan shares a 900-kilometer border with Iran. They are literal neighbors. Iran has attacked countries far less threatening to it — Jordan, Turkey, Oman, Cyprus — countries with no shared border and minimal strategic significance to the US campaign. Yet Pakistan, which borders Iran directly, which has US reconnaissance assets on its territory, which has deployed F-16s to Saudi Arabia under a mutual defense pact — has not received a single Iranian strike. Iran has also not attacked Pakistan verbally. No threats. No warnings. No ultimatums. In a war where Iran has threatened everyone from the UK to South Korea — complete silence toward Pakistan. Here's why... 1. Pakistan is playing every side simultaneously — and Iran knows it. Pakistan finds itself in one of the most complex positions of any country on earth right now. It has a strategic defense agreement with Saudi Arabia — Iran's regional rival. It has deployed F-16s to Saudi soil. It procures over 80% of its military weapons from China. It is simultaneously fighting its own war against the Taliban on its Afghan border. It is managing violent pro-Iran Shia protests inside its own cities. It has evacuated approximately 35,000 Pakistani nationals trapped inside Iran. And it has publicly stated it considers Iran to be "defending itself" against US-Israeli aggression. Pakistan is simultaneously allied with Iran's enemies and sympathetic to Iran's cause. Attacking Pakistan would force it to pick a side. And right now — Pakistan not picking a side is more valuable to Iran than any missile strike could achieve. 2. China. This is where it gets strategically important. China has invested $62 billion in the China-Pakistan Economic Corridor — CPEC. A massive infrastructure project running from western China all the way to Gwadar Port on the Arabian Sea in Pakistan's Balochistan province. Gwadar sits just 170 kilometers from Iran's own port of Chabahar. China has been clear in its position: the CPEC corridor and Gwadar Port must be protected at all costs. Beijing has even proposed permanently stationing Chinese military personnel in Gwadar. Iran attacking Pakistan means Iran attacking the endpoint of China's most important strategic infrastructure project. China buys over 80% of Iran's oil exports. It is Iran's single most critical economic lifeline during this war. Iran will not bite the hand that feeds it. 3. The Corridor Theory. This is an analytical hypothesis — not confirmed fact — but it is being discussed seriously by defense analysts. Iran has been firing thousands of missiles and drones every day for 16 days. The US has destroyed Iran's missile production facilities. Bombed its military infrastructure. Claims Iran's missile volume is down 90% from Day 1. So the question that genuinely puzzles analysts is: where are Iran's weapons still coming from? One theory gaining traction: the CPEC corridor running through Pakistan's Balochistan province — which shares a border with Iran's Sistan-Balochistan province — may be functioning as a supply route. Oil going from Iran into China via Pakistan. Drones, missiles and military supplies coming back the other way. CPEC assets in Balochistan must be "urgently protected" — while simultaneously acknowledging the corridor's strategic proximity to Iran. If this route exists — attacking Pakistan destroys the very lifeline keeping Iran's war machine running. 4. The nuclear factor. Pakistan is a nuclear-armed state. Iran is not. Attacking a nuclear power — even with conventional weapons — carries escalation risks no military planner takes lightly. A conflict that spills into Pakistani territory risks triggering responses that could involve China, India, and nuclear calculations that dwarf everything happening in the Gulf right now. Iran is fighting a calculated, strategic war. Not a reckless one. Starting a nuclear-adjacent crisis with Pakistan while already fighting the US and Israel simultaneously is not strategy. It is suicide. Here is what all four reasons point to when you put them together. Iran has not attacked Pakistan because Pakistan — whether intentionally or not — sits at the intersection of every strategic interest Iran needs to protect. China's money. China's infrastructure. People need to understand what doxxing actually is. Laws vary from state to state, but basically doxxing can create civil liability if: 1. Personal information is published about a person electronically. 2. Without that person's consent. 3. With the intent to harass or intimidate. That's it. It can create criminal liability if the victim also reasonably fears for his or her life, or the life of his or her family. (Again, this varies by state.) There is this weird misconception on the part of some amateur, childlike Perry Masons that if personal information is out there somewhere else on the Internet already, than exposing that information is not doxxing. That's incorrect. It's that malicious intent that matters. Imagine you are in a huge argument with another X poster. It's gotten ugly. That person uses their real name. Suppose you find their property tax info pre-existing elsewhere on the Internet and you post their address with malicious intent. You just doxxed that person legally. It does not matter that the property info was available elsewhere on the Internet. Everyone please be careful out there--it's too easy to get in trouble. Don't let emotion over X flame wars put you in a position you don't want to be in.

On the Iditarod Trail, winter conditions can change mile by mile. River ice thickens and thins. Snow bridges form and collapse. Glaciers shift. What looks solid one day may change the next. Because when travel depends on frozen rivers and valleys, reading the landscape matters. 📸 1: Aerial photo showing fracture line of avalanche along a snow ridge line. A reminder of how quickly conditions can shift in steep terrain. 📸 2: Steam rises through fractured ice at Redoubt Volcano, where heat from below reshapes the frozen surface above. 📸 3: View of Nellie Juan Glacier from Wolverine Glacier, where visibility and weather can change in minutes. An interesting perspective Raz Zimmt (@RZimmt) A few remarks regarding the Israeli perspective that may explain the continuation of the policy of decapitating senior Iranian officials. One can agree with it or oppose it, but it is worth at least understanding it, because it will also influence the continuation of the campaign. From Israel’s perspective, there is currently no one among the decision-makers in Iran—neither in the political leadership nor in the military establishment—who can be relied upon to bring about a meaningful change in Iranian strategy after the war. In the view of Israeli decision-makers, the distinction between pragmatic conservatives such as Larijani and hardliners such as Ahmad Vahidi may be relevant to academic Iran watchers, but it has little practical significance. Even the supposedly more pragmatic figures were not prepared before the war—and certainly not after it—to implement a “paradigmatic change,” as some of the more moderate voices outside Iran’s decision-making circles had proposed. In addition, since Israel would oppose any future attempt at any arrangement with the Islamic Republic, the question of whether one Iranian official or another might be more or less willing to agree to such a possible arrangement is irrelevant from Israel’s perspective. Given this assessment, the military campaign proceeds from the assumption that the Iranian leadership will likely continue the same policies pursued by the Islamic Republic under Khamenei—perhaps even in a more extreme form—unless Israel’s preferred (and less likely at this stage) scenario materializes: regime change or regime collapse. Therefore, Israel’s assessment focuses on three components: 1. The intentions of the Iranian leadership: Here, as noted, Israel sees no meaningful difference between the different Iranian officials regarding the issues that concern Israel most—nuclear capabilities, missiles, and regional policy. 2. The skills and abilities of the Iranian officials: From this perspective, Larijani may be considered no less dangerous than someone like Saeed Jalili, because he is perceived as having greater influence, experience, and abilities. 3. The military capabilities that will be available to the Iranian leadership after the war: In this context, one can understand the effort to degrade not only Iran’s strategic military capabilities but also its ability to rebuild them after the war. In sum, since Israel cannot ensure that Iran’s leadership after the war will meet the minimum necessary requirements to its national security, any kind of undermining and weakening of the regime—alongside the degradation of its military capabilities—is considered a valid objective. — http://nitter.perennialte.ch/RZimmt/status/2033966174535668059#m

Significa que cada persona puede darse a sí misma la misma compasión que se daría a un buen amigo ante alguna dificultad. GRABACIONES HISTÓRICAS REVELAN EL CANTO DE BALLENAS EN UN OCÉANO SIN CONTAMINACIÓN ACÚSTICA El descubrimiento de la grabación más antigua de ballenas, registrada en marzo de 1949 y recientemente digitalizada, podría transformar el entendimiento sobre la comunicación animal y el entorno sonoro oceánico. Captada por científicos de la Institución Oceanográfica Woods Hole (WHOI) frente a las costas de las Bermudas, esta grabación única da acceso al canto de una ballena jorobada en un océano entonces casi libre de interferencia humana. La importancia de este hallazgo radica en que documenta los sonidos de una ballena en una época donde el océano era mucho más silencioso que en la actualidad. Al ofrecer un registro previo a la contaminación acústica del tráfico naviero y otras actividades humanas, la grabación permite a los científicos estudiar cómo se comunicaban estos animales antes de los cambios ambientales recientes y analizar el impacto del ruido artificial en sus comportamientos. El disco original fue localizado durante la digitalización de archivos históricos en Falmouth, Massachusetts. De acuerdo con Ashley Jester, directora de datos de investigación y servicios de biblioteca en WHOI, los investigadores de la época mantuvieron el equipo registrando incluso en silencio, motivados por la curiosidad científica de captar todo el entorno acústico marino. Esas grabaciones fueron conservadas meticulosamente, lo que posibilitó su hallazgo décadas después, como detalló AP. 📲 Leé la nota completa 🔗 infob.ae/4lI3PZi

This article is compelling and smart. I’ve seen it forwarded around a lot. Let’s walk through why it’s wrong. 1. The author argues that Iran’s military infrastructure especially its drones and missiles are being systematically taken apart. True. But in the aftermath who is going to keep it that way? After the 12 day war Israel and Trump declared Iran’s capacity to make war “obliterated” and set back for a generation. Less than a year later they went back to war because of how quickly Iran was rebuilding. This campaign is much more comprehensive, but the same problem still applies. How to avoid being stuck in the aftermath in a “mow the lawn” scenario where the US has to expend tremendous assets that could be directed elsewhere in the world - especially towards the Indopacific. And where the region operates at a new unstable normal where all previous taboos on military action are off. 2. He argues that the nuclear infrastructure had to be disassembled because one president after another had just let Iran’s nuclear program grow. Not true. Obama had managed to dramatically and verifiably reduce Iran’s nuclear capacity through the JCPOA. Trump killed that. 3. He argues Iran is self harming by stopping its own oil from going through the Strait of Hormuz. This was always an assumption before the war, but they’ve managed to shut down the Strait for everyone else while still exporting 1 million bbls per day of their own stuff. That makes this much more sustainable. 4. He Argues that Iran’s proxy networks are dramatically weakened. True, but also as we’ve learned from previous conflicts they will regenerate and it’s impossible to root them out with a military strategy alone if there is no political follow up to create a better alternative. That is why Israel is on the verge of a major campaign in Lebanon only a year and a half after supposedly setting back Hezbollah for a generation. These fights are costly Pyrrhic victories that will just need to be fought again and again and again unless there is a political strategy to consolidate victory which both Israel and the US have failed at since October 7th. 5. Finally, the author argues that we need to ignore the President’s own words about regime change and the Iranian people rising up and focus on what the military is doing. But that’s not how war works. War is fought to achieve a political objective. If there is no clear objective set out by the political leadership it’s impossible to translate battlefield victories into a consolidated win. By setting the bar at regime change Trump has made it extraordinarily hard for the US to be perceived as winning even if the military executes the plans. Perception is a big part of the battle in war. And again the costs are incredibly high. And as the author argues, the only way this works is if there is a plan to contain and keep Iran down in the aftermath. Do we have any faith in Trump to do that? Again that is going to be incredibly expensive and require a presence like what the US left in the Middle East after the first Gulf War to contain Saddam. That’s something we could afford in 1991 when the US was a unipolar power. But not in 2026 when we have a real competitor in China that we need to manage. aljazeera.com/amp/opinions/2…

Each March, mushers and sled dogs prepare to travel one of Alaska’s most historic winter routes during the Iditarod Trail Sled Dog Race. The trail itself isn’t permanent. It takes shape each winter. The depth, density, and timing of snowpack determine when a winter trail can safely take shape across public lands, including sections managed by the Bureau of Land Management. Small shifts in temperature can mean thinner snow at lower elevations or earlier melt in key sections. In fact, low snow has forced the Iditarod to move its starting location in 2003, 2015, 2017, and again in 2025. USGS scientists track snow conditions from satellites and in the field to better understand how Alaska’s winter landscape changes from year to year. On 28th February 2026, the final electoral roll of Bengal stood at 7,04,59,284 electors. Out of these, nearly 60 lakh electors were placed under arbitrary adjudication. Their names remain part of the final electoral roll until and unless they are explicitly rejected by the designated judicial officers or the Appellate Tribunals. In these circumstances, the notification issued on 15th March 2026 should have clearly shown the total figure of 7,04,59,284, with a bold asterisk or clarification stating that approximately 60 lakh electors are under verification and their fate will be decided through subsequent supplementary lists. Instead, the Election Commission deliberately slashed the number and declared only 6,44,52,609 electors, without any explanation, without any asterisk, without any transparency. This is a calculated, fraudulent attempt by @BJP4India and their B-team to erase 60 lakh Bengali voters from the democratic process and create mass confusion. Video

We have full faith in the Judiciary and in the ability of Judicial Officers to deliver justice as per the clear directions of the Supreme Court. But where is the urgency from the Election Commission? The Supreme Court gave express orders to publish supplementary lists in a timely manner for the 60 lakh voters kept under arbitrary adjudication. That order has been brazenly violated by @ECISVEEP. The Supreme Court also constituted Appellate Tribunals to hear grievances. Yet, without the supplementary lists, 60 lakh people are being kept completely in the dark about their own voting status. Our three-member delegation met the Chief Electoral Officer, West Bengal, and submitted a formal representation flagging serious procedural lapses that strike at the very core of electoral transparency and citizens’ rights. 👉 Discrepancy in Elector Count: The official notification dated 15th March 2026 records a significantly lower voter count, ignoring nearly 60 lakh electors placed under adjudication, whose names, by law, must continue in the rolls until due determination. This misrepresentation undermines transparency and public trust. 👉 Non-Publication of Supplementary Rolls: Despite ongoing verifications and clear directions from the Hon’ble Supreme Court, supplementary electoral rolls have not been published. This denies voters clarity on their status and effectively blocks their ability to seek legal remedies. 👉 Non-Operational Appellate Tribunals: Even as names are being deleted, the mandated appellate mechanism remains non-functional, depriving citizens of their rightful avenue for redress and violating principles of natural justice. These are systemic failures that risk disenfranchising lakhs of voters. We have demanded immediate corrective action to uphold the integrity, transparency, and credibility of the electoral process.

New milestone for ANGEO-1🇦🇴 : work has officially begun at our site in Toulouse, France. Based on our next generation S250 optical satellite, ANGEO-1 will be the first Angolan, very high performance Earth observation satellite. It will be the most advanced satellite in its class in the region, positioning Angola as a leading space power. The ANGEO-1 programme will further foster the development of the country in many different sectors such as: ➡️ Infrastructure development ➡️ Mapping of natural resources ➡️ Maritime surveillance including fisheries ➡️ Agriculture It will also provide a better understanding of the origins and impacts of climate change on the economy, such as drought monitoring, rising sea levels and water resources. This will lead to being better prepared in case of natural disasters with improved response rates and reduced loss of assets. Image: Luanda, the capital city of Angola seen from space 🛰️

IoT-Driven Water Management in Rural Tamil Nadu In Erode district, Tamil Nadu, an IoT-enabled smart water management system has been introduced to improve efficiency in rural water supply networks. Using sensors to monitor tank levels and automate pump operations, the system enables real-time management of overhead tanks and prevents overflow, ensuring more reliable water distribution. Deployed across 50 habitations in 16 villages, the solution has delivered a 40% reduction in electricity costs, 50% lower electricity consumption, and a 20% increase in water supply. In Ponmudi village alone, daily water availability increased by 44,180 litres. The initiative demonstrates how technology-led, institution-driven solutions can improve water efficiency, reduce operational costs, and strengthen sustainable rural infrastructure. ریاست هواشناسی وزارت ترانسپورت و هوانوردی طالبان احتمال بارش برف و باران را در ۲۴ ولایت کشور پیش‌بینی کرده است‌. براساس پیش‌بینی این ریاست، فردا (چهارشنبه، ۲۷ حوت) ولایت‌های قندهار، زابل، ارزگان، دایکندی، غزنی، میدان وردک، پکتیا، پکتیکا، خوست، لوگر، کابل، پروان، کاپیسا، بغلان، بدخشان، قندوز، سمنگان، بامیان، بلخ، سرپل، جوزجان، فاریاب، بادغیس و غور شاهد بارندگی خواهند بود. ریاست هواشناسی طالبان میزان بارش برف را در این ولایت‌ها بین ۱۰ تا ۳۰ سانتی‌متر و میزان بارش باران را بین ۱۰ تا ۳۰ میلی‌متر پیش‌بینی کرده است. این ریاست همچنین احتمال وزش باد با سرعت ۵۰ تا ۷۰ کیلومتر در ساعت را برای ولایت‌های جنوبی ‌و احتمال سرازیرشدن سیلاب‌ را در مناطق گرمسیر پیش‌بینی کرده است.

هیأت معاونت سازمان ملل متحد در افغانستان (یوناما) در پی حملهٔ هوایی شب گذشتهٔ پاکستان بر شفاخانهٔ معتادان در شهر کابل، با ابراز تسلیت عمیق به خانواده‌های قربانیان و آرزوی بهبودی برای زخمی‌ها، این رویداد را مایه نگرانی جدی خوانده و بر ضرورت حفاظت از افراد ملکی در جریان درگیری‌ها تأکید کرده است. یوناما بدون ارایه جزییات نوشته است که در این حمله ده‌ها تن شهید و زخمی شده‌اند. منبع نگاشته است که بر مبنای قوانین بین‌المللی بشردوستانه، تمامی طرف‌های درگیر مکلف‌اند از افراد ملکی، بیماران، کارکنان صحی و شفاخانه‌ها محافظت کنند و هرگونه حمله بر تأسیسات صحی و اهداف ملکی به‌گونه صریح ممنوع است. این نهاد افزوده است که افراد ملکی همچنان بهای درگیری‌های جاری میان افغانستان و پاکستان را می‌پردازند و یوناما از ۲۶ فبروری تا ۱۶ مارچ، شهید شدن دست‌کم ۷۶ فرد ملکی و زخمی شدن ۲۱۳ تن دیگر را در نتیجه این تنش‌ها ثبت کرده است. یوناما بار دیگر خواستار کاهش فوری تنش‌ها و برقراری آتش‌بس شده و هر دو طرف درگیر خواسته است تا به تعهدات خود در قبال قوانین بین‌المللی پابند مانده و از غیرنظامیان حفاظت کنند.

Let’s look at how President Dr Arif Alvi (@ArifAlvi) ran the Presidency during the austerity drive. When Pakistan faced severe economic pressure, Imran Khan’s government directed all state institutions to cut costs. This wasn’t just lip service. The austerity drive was actually implemented — not followed by buying fleets of luxury vehicles or Gulfstream jets while preaching restraint. The Presidency followed through. The President House budget was reduced by ~50%, falling from about Rs 963M in earlier years to Rs 507M in FY2020-21. Since then, spending has steadily climbed back up: • 2020-21 — Rs 507M (austerity peak) • 2021-22 — Rs 528M • 2022-23 — Rs 600M • 2023-24 — Rs 624M • 2024-25 — Rs 855M • 2025-26 — Rs 933M The numbers tell a simple story: Austerity → then a return to the old spending levels. The discovery of californium was announced 76 years ago on this day, after it was synthesized by a team of physicists at the University of California Radiation Laboratory in Berkeley @UCBerkeley. Each microgram of fresh californium produces 139 million neutrons per minute, which makes it a strong neutron emitter. This makes californium useful for some nuclear reactors that rely on neutrons as a start-up source for chain reactions. These californium-emitted neutrons are also an effective tool in healthcare. They can be used to treat certain types of cervical and brain cancers, particularly when other radiation therapies are ineffective.

It needs to be noted that Seven Member Bench of the Supreme Court of Pakistan in Malik Qayyum Case (reported in 2001 PLD SC 568) held that bias on part of the judge vitiates judicial proceedings. The court further held that an accused has a right of a fair trial by a judicial minded person, not by someone functioning under an influence or bias as the same paralyses his judicial faculties to conduct fair trial. Bias would vitiate judicial proceedings if such circumstances exist. Bias robs the judge of the confidence that a litigant may have in the judge. Court further held that bias is mental disposition or attitude towards a particular person and covers all kind of hostilities and prejudices against him.

We are pleased to welcome Dr. Atindra Nath Mondal to the Trinamool Congress family. A distinguished medical professional and seasoned public health administrator, he currently serves as the Additional Medical Superintendent at the College of Medicine & JNM Hospital, Kalyani, in Nadia. Over the years, he has held several key administrative positions, including Medical Superintendent of Ranaghat Sub-Divisional Hospital and Deputy Medical Superintendent at SSKM Hospital, Kolkata. With a strong academic foundation, holding an MBBS and DPH from Calcutta University, along with an MBA in Hospital Administration, he brings with him extensive experience in managing healthcare institutions across both rural and urban settings. His career reflects a deep understanding of public health systems and a sustained commitment to improving healthcare delivery. We extend a warm welcome and look forward to his valuable contributions in further strengthening our collective efforts towards people-centric progress.

🌋 40 years of Mount Etna eruptions through the eyes of our satellites 📍 Mount Etna — Sicily, Italy In the 1980s, when Etna erupted, we watched from afar. Limited resolution and revisit times. Days before data could be fully analysed. The volcano was active, but our eyes in space were still learning to see. Today, the volcano still stands, but in a completely different technological era. Our Earth observation ecosystem is now much faster, sharper and smarter. Thanks to satellite imagery, we’ve been able to track four decades of eruptions, lava flows, and landscape transformations with unprecedented precision: 📈 Better understanding volcanic dynamics ⚡ Anticipating risks 🚒 Protecting communities and infrastructure 🔬 Supporting scientific research 👇📸 These SPOT satellite images of Mount Etna, captured between 1989 and 2025, are more than a geological timeline. What makes them truly fascinating is not only the volcanic activity itself, but also the technological revolution behind these images seen from space. As a bonus, the last snapshot below is an Amplitude Change Detection image. Created from 4 individual acquisitions performed by our Radar Constellation, its colorisation shows the structural changes of the volcano’s surface between 2008 and 2019. 📸 Want to explore the SPOT 6 image in full resolution? Kasaragod is the northern gateway of Keralam and an important railway corridor connecting the state with Karnataka and the rest of India. Unfortunately, despite heavy passenger movement, railway connectivity in this region remains extremely inadequate. The people of Kasaragod are not asking for luxury trains or prestigious announcements. Their demand is simple—basic train services, proper stoppages, and reliable connectivity. I would like to place some important demands before the government: • There is an urgent need to introduce MEMU commuter services between Kannur and Mangalore, or Kozhikode and Mangalore, to support thousands of daily passengers. • The Palakkad–Kannur evening special train departing from Kozhikode should be extended up to Kasaragod or Mangalore. • Parasuram Express must be given stoppages at Kottikulam , Kumbla, and Trikaripur stations. • Trains that currently terminate at Kannur must be extended to Kasargod or Mangalore. • The government should introduce Jan Shatabdi Express services in this region, considering the heavy passenger demand. • The Antyodaya Express should be operated daily to support long-distance unreserved passengers. • Passenger trains such as the Shoranur Passenger and Coimbatore Passenger should be extended up to Kasaragod and Manjeswaram. • The Amrit Bharat station development projects at Kanhangad and Nileshwaram must be implemented without delay. • Kumbla railway station with 30 acres of land must be upgraded as a terminal station with proper passenger facilities. • Ticket reservation counters should be reinstalled in many railway stations like Kottikulam. • The Kasaragod - Byndoor Mookambika Road Passenger (No. 56665–56666), suspended since 2008, should be restored. : @RajmohanUnnitha ji in Lok Sabha Video

The state of the UK's armed forces, once the envy of empires, is now a fading shadow of its former self. It's so hollowed out that the British Army has only about 50,000 medically deployable soldiers out of a total of 73,000, making it the smallest since the Napoleonic Wars. It's also shrinking further, with net 300 soldiers leaving each month. With reserves, the UK could currently mobilize 180,000. Maybe you think this doesn't sound so bad. Let me put these numbers in context. My home country of Singapore (a former British colony) is a tiny island nation state with a population of 6 million. The UK's is more than 10X larger at 68 million. Yet, the Singapore Armed Forces has 51,000 full-time active personnel and it can mobilize a total force of >300,000 (with reserves). That's 300,00 for a population of 6 million (Singapore) compared to 180,000 for a population of 68 million (UK). Now also consider: > The Royal Navy has shrunk by 75% since the 1982 Falklands War > ammunition stockpiles are so low that the Army has enough for only a light brigade to deploy and fight briefly > all 19 howitzers have been handed over to Ukraine; the Army now relies on temporary loans while waiting for replacements > Submarine readiness is threadbare: Only 0-2 Astute-class attack subs are available at any time (vs. the expected 3-5), forcing patrols to stretch over 200 days, with crews scavenging food and facing medicine shortages > The frigate fleet is down to 13 operational escorts (below the required 19), with one Type-45 destroyer sidelined for over eight years and another (HMS Lancaster) scrapped overseas because it was so worn out it couldn't even make the journey home > Recruitment is in crisis: the British Army hit just 63% of targets last year, with a 12 month gap from application to training > only one in 10 applicants succeed; just 11% of 18-27-year-olds would risk their lives for the country Budget cuts, bureaucratic rot, and political cowardice - this is more than managed decline. It's symptomatic of the malaise plaguing Britain on ALL fronts. Countries in the Middle East are not fully prepared to repel such massive attacks. This is what I'm trying to get across – to stop Russia means stopping many different wars. From an interview with i24NEWS and Jerusalem Post (3/3).

Answering a question about the Iranian regime’s threats to Ukraine over our support for the Gulf countries. This is nothing new. I have heard many different messages over the last four years. What’s important for us is that the United States and leaders of Middle Eastern countries asked for help with drone interceptors. They sought our expertise in air defense. Air defense is not about offensive capabilities. That's why I said that we were ready to help with this expertise and defensive systems. We are not afraid of any messages of the kind. We have heard such messages every day for the last four years, for 12 years, to be precise. It's not new for us. From an interview with i24NEWS and Jerusalem Post (2/3).

The first night of the full-scale war began with missiles. Russia went all-in with everything they had: cruise, ballistic, and other types of missiles. They attacked us from Russia and from Belarus. It was terrible, but after some time we found out how to intercept missiles and protect people, energy system and other infrastructure. In the meantime, the Iranian regime supplied Russia with the first batch of “shaheds” – 1,000 drones. We got in touch with the Iranians at the level of intelligence services. We asked them not to supply weapons to Russia, because if the supplied “shaheds” had killed our civilians, the Iranian regime would become Russia’s ally, we told them. They responded, “No-no, we are not allies in this. We sold the Russians this one batch of “shaheds”. It will be 1,200 or 1,300 drones, and that's it. No more supplies.” But they lied. They gave them not only thousands of these drones, they gave them licenses to produce “shahed” type drones. They helped Russia to build two factories which produce these drones, and initially they operated the drones and trained the Russians. From an interview with i24NEWS and Jerusalem Post (1/3).

Al Jazeera claims, based on estimated figures from the 12-day war, that Iran possessed up to 2,500 missiles at the start of that conflict. I don’t even know where to begin, because both ends of that claim are wrong, both the 2,500 estimate itself and the assumption that the post-12-day-war inventory has remained unchanged until today. Any analysis of another country’s military inventory must be based on production timelines, supply chains, and comparative industrial capacity. North Korea, whose missile industry is roughly one-third the size of Iran’s, is capable of commissioning up to 1,000 missiles in a single ceremony. Estimates suggest Russia produces around 2,500-3,000 missiles per year. And Iran? The Persians began producing missiles in the late 1980s and early 1990s. Since then, they have never stopped stockpiling. In the eight months since the end of the 12-day war, if Iran had done nothing but refurbishing old missiles, factoring in its domestic fuel production, it would already have added 700-1,000 missiles to its stockpile. But Iran has done far more than that. The most likely scenario is that, in this same period, it has added 2 to 4 times that number. Iran is a missile country. They don’t have a decent air force, or strong navy or armored vehicles. They are focused on missiles. Iran currently manufactures around 15–20 different models and variants of ballistic and cruise missiles, including anti-ship missiles. How many of each model does it produce annually? And it has been simultaneously producing more than 10 models for over a decade. How many missiles do you think it has accumulated? Certainly far more than 2,500. The reduction in Iranian launches is due to the destruction or burial of silos and launch ramps in successive coalition strikes, but also by deliberate choice, a strategy of prolonged war of attrition. In this phase, production will be deliberately kept low and resources carefully rationed. The exact same thing is happening with the US and Israel. Their main shortages are interceptors and precision-guided munitions, two categories that take a long time to manufacture. Iran has a much larger stocks of SRBMs on top of that that can hit the gulf, reported at 6,000-8000 by @IranWonk, although I am still waiting for confirmation on the source(s). China was the first country to establish diplomatic relations with Turkmenistan. It was also among the earliest supporters of Turkmenistan's policy of permanent neutrality and the first to formalize a strategic partnership with the country through a political document. The friendship between the two nations dates back more than 2,000 years. Along the ancient Silk Road, Chinese silk and porcelain reached Central Asia, while Turkmenistan's famed Akhal-Teke horse, known in China as the "sweat blood horse," became a symbol of early exchanges between the two peoples. Modern diplomatic ties began on January 6, 1992, when the two countries signed a joint statement and established ambassadorial relations. Today, cooperation continues to deepen in culture, education, media and sports. Local partnerships are also growing, including the sister province relationship between northwest China's Shaanxi Province and Turkmenistan's Mary region. From the Silk Road to today, China and Turkmenistan continue to write new chapters of friendship built on mutual respect and shared development. IoT-Driven Water Management in Rural Tamil Nadu In Erode district, Tamil Nadu, an IoT-enabled smart water management system has been introduced to improve efficiency in rural water supply networks. Using sensors to monitor tank levels and automate pump operations, the system enables real-time management of overhead tanks and prevents overflow, ensuring more reliable water distribution. Deployed across 50 habitations in 16 villages, the solution has delivered a 40% reduction in electricity costs, 50% lower electricity consumption, and a 20% increase in water supply. In Ponmudi village alone, daily water availability increased by 44,180 litres. The initiative demonstrates how technology-led, institution-driven solutions can improve water efficiency, reduce operational costs, and strengthen sustainable rural infrastructure. I decided to kind of spice things up a bit and pivot to malware defense stuff. I explored different thingies and fell down the rabbit hole of YARA stuff. I didn't want to dive into something like minifilters. I've got this goofy setup where I can extract YARA rules from Windows Defender because of the research from @_t_tani. I've got like, 20,000 YARA rules, or something, I don't know. It's a lot. Regardless, I was like, "maybe I should make a shrimple file scanner with all these YARA rules". This is what a basic static analysis engine does in usermode. I saw a lot of people being like, "JUST YARA.EXE --FILE", and I was like, "that's kind of lame". I started bonking the YARA open source repo looking at different stuff. I then had to fight YARA open source stuff because libyara64.lib wants to fight you to become libyara64.dll. People on GitHub complained too, but whatever, I figured it out. My next goal is transform all the YARA rules into YARAC, or whatever it's called. In theory, I could then take a binary, or directory, and then use the YARA analysis engine to compare it to all the Microsoft YARA rules. I then considered implementing basic parameters, or maybe a goofy ass UI, or something. I then realized I'm basically making THORLite-Lite.

अफगानिस्तान और पाकिस्तान के बीच चल रहा सीमा विवाद थमने का नाम नहीं ले रहा. सीमा पर हालात तनावपूर्ण हैं. 17 मार्च को अफगानिस्तान ने आरोप लगाया कि पाकिस्तान ने सोमवार देर रात काबुल के एक अस्पताल पर एयर स्ट्राइक की है, जिसमें 400 लोगों की दर्दनाक मौत हो गई. इस खबर ने हर किसी को झकझोर कर रख दिया है. अस्पताल पर हुए इस हमले को अफगानिस्तान के स्टार क्रिकेटर और कप्तान राशिद खान ने 'युद्ध अपराध' (War Crime) करार दिया है. राशिद खान ने सोशल मीडिया पर एक पोस्ट में अपना दर्द शेयर किया. उन्होंने कहा कि रमजान के पवित्र महीने में इस तरह का नरसंहार न केवल मानवता के खिलाफ है, बल्कि नफरत की आग को और भड़काने वाला है. राशिद के साथ-साथ अनुभवी ऑलराउंडर मोहम्मद नबी ने भी इस हमले की निंदा की है. बताया जा रहा है कि जिस अस्पताल में नशे की लत से जूझ रहे युवाओं का इलाज किया जा रहा था, वह पाकिस्तान की एयरस्ट्राइक से तबाह हो गया है. राशिद ने इस हमले की निंदा करते हुए अंतरराष्ट्रीय मानवाधिकार संगठनों से इस 'अत्याचार' की निष्पक्ष जांच की मांग की है. राशिद खान ने X पर लिखा कि 'मैं काबुल में पाकिस्तानी एयरस्ट्राइक के कारण नागरिकों के हताहत होने की ताजा रिपोर्ट से बेहद दुखी हूं. नागरिक घरों, शैक्षणिक संस्थानों या मेडिकल इंफ्रास्ट्रक्चर को निशाना बनाना, चाहे जानबूझकर हो या गलती से, एक युद्ध अपराध है. मानव जीवन के प्रति इतनी बड़ी अनदेखी, खासकर रमजान के पवित्र महीने में, बेहद पीड़ादायक और चिंताजनक है.' राशिद खान ने अपनी पोस्ट में आगे लिखा है कि 'यह सिर्फ विभाजन और नफरत को बढ़ाएगा. मैं संयुक्त राष्ट्र और अन्य मानवाधिकार एजेंसियों से अपील करता हूं कि वे इस घटना की गहराई से जांच करें और दोषियों को जवाबदेह ठहराएं. मैं इस कठिन समय में अपने अफगान लोगों के साथ खड़ा हूं. हम ठीक होंगे और एक राष्ट्र के रूप में फिर उठ खड़े होंगे. हम हमेशा ऐसा करते हैं.' #RashidKhan #PakistanAfghanistanConflict #Kabul #Hospital #Airstrike #Taliban #Pakistan #MiddleEast #Afghanistan #ZeeNews

বেগম খালেদা জিয়ার নামাজে জানাজায় নারীদের জন্য বিশেষ ব্যবস্থা ঢাকা, ৩০ ডিসেম্বর ২০২৫: বাংলাদেশ জাতীয়তাবাদী দল (বিএনপি)-এর চেয়ারপার্সন, তিনবারের সাবেক প্রধানমন্ত্রী ও গণতান্ত্রিক রাজনীতির শীর্ষ নেত্রী বেগম খালেদা জিয়ার ইন্তেকালে দেশব্যাপী গভীর শোকের আবহ বিরাজ করছে। তাঁর প্রতি শেষ শ্রদ্ধা জানাতে সর্বস্তরের মানুষের অংশগ্রহণ নিশ্চিত করতে প্রয়োজনীয় প্রস্তুতি গ্রহণ করা হয়েছে অন্তর্বর্তীকালীন সরকার। এই প্রেক্ষাপটে বেগম খালেদা জিয়ার নামাজে জানাজায় অংশগ্রহণ করতে ইচ্ছুক নারীদের জন্য বিশেষ ব্যবস্থা রাখা হয়েছে। জাতীয় সংসদ ভবনের দক্ষিণ প্লাজা ও মানিক মিয়া এভিনিউ এলাকায় নারীদের জন্য পৃথকভাবে এ বিশেষ ব্যবস্থা করা হয়েছে, যাতে তাঁরা সুশৃঙ্খল ও নিরাপদ পরিবেশে জানাজায় অংশ নিতে পারেন। উল্লেখ্য, বেগম খালেদা জিয়ার নামাজে জানাজা বাদ জোহর বেলা দুইটায় অনুষ্ঠিত হবে। জানাজায় অংশগ্রহণে আগ্রহী সকলকে নিরাপত্তাজনিত কারণে কোনো প্রকার ব্যাগ বহন না করার জন্য অনুরোধ জানানো হচ্ছে। বেগম খালেদা জিয়াকে শেষ বিদায় জানাতে আগত সকলের সার্বিক নিরাপত্তা ও শৃঙ্খলা নিশ্চিত করতে সংশ্লিষ্ট কর্তৃপক্ষ প্রয়োজনীয় সব ধরনের ব্যবস্থা গ্রহণ করেছে।

❇️पारंपरिक कलाकारों, लोक कलाकारों और सांस्कृतिक संस्थानों को वित्तीय सहायता ❇️संस्कृति मंत्रालय देश भर में पारंपरिक एवं लोक कलाओं सहित विभिन्न प्रकार की प्रदर्शन कलाओं से जुड़े संगठनों/कलाकारों को वित्तीय सहायता प्रदान करने के लिए कला संस्कृति विकास योजना (केएसवीवाई) का संचालन करता है। ❇️यह एक केन्‍द्रीय क्षेत्र की योजना है, जिसमें विभिन्न योजना घटक शामिल हैं। इन योजनाओं का संक्षिप्त विवरण परिशिष्ट में दिया गया है। -यह जानकारी केन्‍द्रीय संस्कृति एवं पर्यटन मंत्री गजेन्‍द्र सिंह शेखावत ने आज लोकसभा में एक प्रश्‍न के लिखित उत्तर में दी। विवरण: pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.… @MinOfCultureGoI

This Day, That Year. Taking you back 12 summers. On 17 March, 2011, a shocking revelation linked to WikiLeaks sent ripples across India’s political landscape. Leaked diplomatic cables alleged that during the crucial 2008 trust vote in the Parliament of India, allies of the ruling Congress leadership displayed chests of cash to secure MPs’ support and save the government of Manmohan Singh. The vote was meant to test the government’s legitimacy after the controversial India–US nuclear deal. Instead, it became synonymous with the “cash-for-votes” scandal, a moment when the sanctity of Parliament was overshadowed by allegations that money was used to influence elected representatives. Today in San José, Costa Rica, I had the honor of opening the Ninth Assembly of the OAS Inter-American Telecommunication Commission @OEA_CITEL. I thanked the Government of Costa Rica @micittcr for hosting this important gathering and recognized the continued commitment of @OAS_official Member States, regulators, industry, academia, and the technical community to advancing connectivity across the Americas. Communication and connectivity have long been central to the inter-American system. As early as the First International American Conference in 1890, our countries envisioned linking the Hemisphere through shared communications infrastructure. Today, through CITEL, the Organization of American States continues that tradition by strengthening regional cooperation on telecommunications and digital technologies. Telecommunications are no longer simply a sector of the economy; they are the backbone of modern society. Expanding meaningful connectivity, modernizing regulatory frameworks, and strengthening digital ecosystems are essential for innovation, education, healthcare, and democratic participation throughout our region. The San José Declaration reflects the shared commitment of our Member States to advance universal connectivity, resilient digital infrastructure, and stronger collaboration among governments, industry, academia, and civil society. Through dialogue and partnership, we can build a more connected, innovative, and inclusive Americas.

UNA INESPERADA CONEXIÓN ENTRE EL POLEN, LA INMUNIDAD Y LA EXTINCIÓN DE LOS MAMUTS SORPRENDE A LA CIENCIA El hallazgo de restos de mamuts con indicios de alergia al polen ha generado nuevas hipótesis sobre las causas de su desaparición. Un equipo de investigadores de Austria, Rusia e Israel, respaldados por instituciones académicas en sus respectivos países, detectó fragmentos de inmunoglobulina en fósiles, lo que sugiere que estos animales pudieron haber desarrollado enfermedades alérgicas graves cuando la concentración de polen aumentó durante el deshielo global. Según un artículo publicado en la revista científica Earth History and Biodiversity —especializada en paleobiología y estudios evolutivos— y difundido por Muy Interesante, la presencia anómala de inmunoglobulinas, proteínas asociadas a respuestas alérgicas, coincidía con periodos de mayor abundancia de polen en los registros paleoclimáticos. Los restos analizados proceden de yacimientos en Siberia, donde las condiciones de conservación permitieron el estudio detallado de moléculas biológicas que normalmente no sobreviven al paso del tiempo. 📲 Leé la nota completa 🔗 infob.ae/41abCW4

On this day in 1959, the first nuclear reactor built solely for the purpose of medical research reached criticality. Operating at three megawatts thermal, the Brookhaven Medical Research Reactor (BMRR) at @BrookhavenLab was many times smaller than most power reactors. It was primarily used for research into a radiotherapy technique known as boron neutron capture therapy (BNCT). BNCT involves the selective targeting of cancer cells by irradiating boron compounds which have been placed within tumours. This treatment may be effective in treating brain cancers, such as glioblastoma multiforme. After years of supporting scientific research, the BMRR was shut down in December 2000.

Foreign kingdoms that did not share with him lineage, language, or culture still submitted to his message while never seeing him. What influence are you even talking about! And no matter how Islamic empires fall, they will rise again and continue, and this will remain until the Day of Resurrection. Look at this influence; look at this greatness. We will die, and every human breathing today will vanish, friend or enemy, but the one who remains is the name of this great man in the hearts of every human soul. Generation after generation will come to sacrifice themselves to raise the banner of monotheism ، the banner of God, the banner of our Prophet Muhammad ﷺ. And after their lives end and they die, their grandchildren will rise again, and so on, until God inherits the earth and all who are upon it. Muhammad is not just a great man; Muhammad is the man who made greatness itself cry at his door for 14 centuries ، and it is still crying, and will cry until the Day of Judgment. This is only his influence ، we haven’t even touched on his life or his prophetic miracles. Even non-Muslim orientalists submitted to his greatness and admitted his truthfulness and extraordinary influence, and placed him first globally. Yes ، after 1400 years, with the crowding of great figures, inventors, and geniuses over hundreds of years, he remained number one in “The 100: A Ranking of the Most Influential Persons in History” ،as testified by his enemies. All the heads of the world at one moment were humbled before a man who died 1000 years ago. He is the only man who broke the definition of “man” completely ،because he was the Messenger of God. Is he powerful? The answer: No ، he is the very power that shaped history with direct divine support. And for this reason, we call this being: the Master of the Universe.

Moscow's ideal scenario for a Middle East war is not a swift victory or a catastrophic escalation, but a conflict of moderate duration and intensity that keeps oil prices high without significantly disrupting the global economy. We are not there yet. Despite the oil windfall, the Kremlin is preparing budget cuts. The one untouchable area – military expenditure – remains predictably unaffected. The Bell (@thebell_io) ✂️ Oil Boom Won’t Shield Russia From Billion-Dollar Spending Cuts Despite the unexpected windfall of a Middle East conflict pushing oil prices higher, the Russian government has begun pressing ahead with sweeping spending cuts worth billions of dollars. “Spending cuts will kill the last bit of economic growth,” a senior official at the Ministry of Economic Development told The Bell. According to Vedomosti, at the start of the year Russia’s Finance Ministry notified all ministries of a 10% across-the-board reduction in spending. Bloomberg estimates the largest possible cut would amount to around 2 trillion rubles ($25 billion), or 0.8% of GDP — though The Bell’s own calculations suggest a more likely range of 0.5–1 trillion rubles ($6–12 billion). So-called “unprotected” budget lines will be first in line for cuts: national projects, infrastructure investment and road construction. Although the Finance Ministry wields considerable authority, sequestration is far from inevitable and is already facing pushback. “The plan is not to cut what is inflated, but what is left — and that’s just crumbs,” said one official at the Ministry of Economic Development. “This year, there is not much room. A transition period could be considered going forward,” a government official agreed. The cuts stem from structural long-term shortfalls. The budget rests on implausibly optimistic assumptions — oil at $59 a barrel, a rate of 92.2 rubles to the dollar — and authorities are banking on $15 billion from a VAT hike that looks increasingly unlikely to materialise amid slowing growth. ➡️ For the first three years of the war, the budget ran fat. Now, with belts tightening and the war still ongoing, civilian spending is the only lever left to pull — even as it has already been squeezed to the bone. — http://nitter.perennialte.ch/thebell_io/status/2033597232268906825#m

Israel is keen to play with fire and this hit will hurt it more than anything it can strike inside Iran. It's a huge escalation though so Iran must be prepared to follow it up with more bold attacks to contain the escalation and control the flow of the war. One possible option is a single warning shot on a non-critical component of the plant. Moscow's ideal scenario for a Middle East war is not a swift victory or a catastrophic escalation, but a conflict of moderate duration and intensity that keeps oil prices high without significantly disrupting the global economy. We are not there yet. Despite the oil windfall, the Kremlin is preparing budget cuts. The one untouchable area – military expenditure – remains predictably unaffected. The Bell (@thebell_io) ✂️ Oil Boom Won’t Shield Russia From Billion-Dollar Spending Cuts Despite the unexpected windfall of a Middle East conflict pushing oil prices higher, the Russian government has begun pressing ahead with sweeping spending cuts worth billions of dollars. “Spending cuts will kill the last bit of economic growth,” a senior official at the Ministry of Economic Development told The Bell. According to Vedomosti, at the start of the year Russia’s Finance Ministry notified all ministries of a 10% across-the-board reduction in spending. Bloomberg estimates the largest possible cut would amount to around 2 trillion rubles ($25 billion), or 0.8% of GDP — though The Bell’s own calculations suggest a more likely range of 0.5–1 trillion rubles ($6–12 billion). So-called “unprotected” budget lines will be first in line for cuts: national projects, infrastructure investment and road construction. Although the Finance Ministry wields considerable authority, sequestration is far from inevitable and is already facing pushback. “The plan is not to cut what is inflated, but what is left — and that’s just crumbs,” said one official at the Ministry of Economic Development. “This year, there is not much room. A transition period could be considered going forward,” a government official agreed. The cuts stem from structural long-term shortfalls. The budget rests on implausibly optimistic assumptions — oil at $59 a barrel, a rate of 92.2 rubles to the dollar — and authorities are banking on $15 billion from a VAT hike that looks increasingly unlikely to materialise amid slowing growth. ➡️ For the first three years of the war, the budget ran fat. Now, with belts tightening and the war still ongoing, civilian spending is the only lever left to pull — even as it has already been squeezed to the bone. — http://nitter.perennialte.ch/thebell_io/status/2033597232268906825#m

Did you know 😏 He rubbed lemon juice on his face. Robbed two banks. Smiled at the cameras. Got caught in an hour. And changed psychology forever. In 1995, McArthur Wheeler walked into two banks in Pittsburgh and robbed them with no mask, no disguise, and lemon juice on his face. He believed that because lemon juice works as invisible ink on paper, it would make his face invisible to cameras. He smiled directly into the security cameras. Police aired the footage on the evening news and arrested him within an hour. When shown the tape, Wheeler stared at the screen and said, "But I wore the juice." He had tested the theory with a Polaroid selfie and didn't appear in the photo — because lemon juice got in his eyes and he aimed the camera at the ceiling. His case inspired Cornell psychologists David Dunning and Justin Kruger to publish their 1999 paper defining the Dunning-Kruger Effect — the cognitive bias where people with low ability drastically overestimate their own competence.

POR QUÉ LA FALTA DE DONANTES DE SANGRE ENCIENDE UNA SEÑAL DE ALERTA EN LOS HOSPITALES DE BUENOS AIRES En una entrevista, Alejandra Vellicce explicó en Infobae al Mediodía que en el Hospital de Clínicas se necesitan entre 30 y 40 donantes de sangre cada día para cubrir la demanda de pacientes, pero advirtió que resulta cada vez más difícil conseguir personas dispuestas a donar por el ritmo de vida actual y la falta de campañas de concientización. Durante su paso por el estudio de Infobae al Mediodía, donde dialogó con Maru Duffard, Andrei Serbin Pont, Jimena Grandinetti, Fede Mayol y Facundo Kablan, la especialista aseguró: “La sangre se necesita todos los días, y a veces estamos tan apurados que no nos ponemos a pensar en la importancia de donar”. La jefa de Hemoterapia explicó que los controles estrictos buscan proteger tanto al donante como al receptor: “Pedimos que pesen más de 50 kilos porque extraemos 450 mililitros, y controlamos con un pinchacito en el dedo si la cantidad de glóbulos rojos es suficiente”. Remarcó que muchos mitos impiden que potenciales voluntarios se acerquen a donar: “No hace falta concurrir en ayunas, esa es una de las causas más habituales de baja presión. Y si tenés tatuajes, solo debe haber pasado seis meses desde el último”. Sobre enfermedades crónicas, detalló: “Por ejemplo, los diabéticos insulino dependientes no pueden donar, pero si no usan insulina sí pueden”. 📲 Leé la nota completa 🔗 infob.ae/4sfrQta

What does Israel get from the Iran war? A prospect of their most powerful, arguably last remaining enemy being decimated by American hands. What the US gets out of it is another question. It was never about the nuclear program. But it wasn't about regime change either. Trump clearly doesn't care about that, as Venezuela's socialist government still in power demonstrates. The "imminent threat" framing is laughable goyslop, same as the tired mantras recycled from 47 years ago. Whatever the 47th president (wink wink) tried to achieve in the opening days of the war, he fell short, unless you consider killing a 90-year-old man and two hundred children a fair exchange for every US military base, greatest ally and vassal in the Middle East getting hit. So what has actually been achieved? Iranians have de facto closed the Strait of Hormuz, and the slow domino collapse of the "global economy" has begun. China, the EU, India, US-aligned East Asian states all depend on Middle Eastern oil. They've already been largely cut off from Russian energy, mostly by US hands. Whether anyone in Washington planned this or simply stumbled into it, either way the consequences are the same: rival economies are being strangled, and eventually they will have to beg the US to turn the tap back on. Or at least, that's what the Trump admin secretly hopes for. Trump meanwhile has "allowed" Russian oil and gas contracts until April and floated plans to "acquire Nord Stream", which they blew up. The logic of controlling the Strait eventually, and with it global energy supply, may well be present somewhere in the room. But it feels less like a master plan and more like someone connecting dots on a map they're drawing as they go, and that map is upside down. The caveats are significant. US troops navigating Iran's mountainous terrain could make Iraq look quaint by comparison, and the 2003-level readiness and troop numbers are simply not there. Trump is hemorrhaging popularity domestically, Democrats will likely take the midterms, and the Gulf state vassals are furious they took hits on America's behalf. The US depends on Taiwanese microchips that get more expensive in an energy crisis, which could halt the entire AI craze and drag the whole damn building with it. At this point, a full US withdrawal from the region isn't hard to imagine. If that were to happen, I truly feel for the Israelis biting their elbows while hiding in their mamads... Either way, I'm rooting for Trump to send as many troops into Iran as possible. Should be a fun and easy ride to Tehran.

Outro pilar estruturante da parceria bilateral é a cooperação energética. Há décadas, a Petrobras ajuda a construir na Bolívia uma das mais importantes experiências de integração energética da América Latina. Em um contexto internacional marcado por conflitos que ameaçam a provisão segura de combustíveis, a Bolívia permanece como uma fonte segura e mantém a condição de maior fornecedor de gás natural para o Brasil. Conversamos sobre a possibilidade de ampliar investimentos nessa área e incrementar o volume exportado para o mercado brasileiro. O Gasoduto Brasil–Bolívia serviu muito ao crescimento da indústria brasileira e do setor de hidrocarbonetos boliviano. Hoje, ele pode ser aproveitado para uma integração mais ampla dos mercados de gás do Cone Sul. Também poderá contribuir para abastecer a fábrica de fertilizantes que o governo boliviano considera instalar em Puerto Quijaro. Também avançamos firmemente rumo à interconexão de nossos sistemas elétricos. O acordo que assinamos hoje abre caminho para a construção de linha de transmissão entre a província de Germán Busch, no departamento de Santa Cruz, e o município de Corumbá. 📸 @ricardostuckert

Somam-se a isso os investimentos robustos que continuamos fazendo para superar a carência de infraestrutura e fomentar a integração física com nossos vizinhos. Em 2004, inaugurei a primeira ponte entre Brasil e Bolívia, ligando Brasiléia, no Acre, a Cobija. Foi preciso aguardar mais de 500 anos para que nossos territórios fossem ligados por uma ponte. Ano passado, assinei a ordem de serviço para construir a segunda ponte entre nossos países, cujas obras terão início em 2027. A ponte sobre o rio Mamoré vai facilitar muito a vida dos moradores de Guajará-Mirim, em Rondônia, e Guayarámerin, no Departamento de Beni. Ela também é peça central para as Rotas de Integração Sul-Americana. Como parte do Quadrante Rondon, vai melhorar a conectividade dos produtores do Brasil e da Bolívia aos portos do Chile e do Peru, permitindo escoamento pelo Oceano Pacífico e acesso aos mercados asiáticos. Também queremos avançar em uma das aspirações que mobilizou vários governos bolivianos: obter acesso fluvial para o Atlântico. Com esse propósito, o Brasil apresentou ano passado projeto de acordo tripartite, com a Bolívia e o Paraguai, para aumento da navegabilidade da hidrovia do rio Paraguai, que inclui a dragagem, sinalização e balizamento do Canal Tamengo, que conecta a Lagoa de Cáceres a Corumbá.

Half Moon Bay’s second-biggest rocket enthusiast. Steve Jurvetson (@FutureJurvetson) 🚀 Today is the 100-year anniversary of the first liquid-fueled rocket launch. Like the Wright Brothers, Robert Goddard’s flight changed rocketry forever, pioneering today's mainstay, liquid-fueled SpaceX rockets. Here are my artifacts from his 1926 flight (last photo). But first, I am pointing to a museum replica of Nell — Goddard’s 10’ tall rocket powered by gasoline and liquid oxygen. It went just 41’ up in 2.5 seconds, hitting 60 MPH, but it marked the dawn of the space age. The New York Times publicly mocked his work in 1920, but Goddard persisted. Fearing further criticism, Goddard kept his 1926 launch secret for nearly a decade. Go Goddard, go, go go! “There can be no thought of finishing, for aiming at the stars, both literally and figuratively, is the work of generations, but no matter how much progress one makes there is always the thrill of just beginning.” — Robert Goddard From the Future Ventures’ space museum, last photo: 1) Inner nozzle from the first flight Starting on the far right, the alundum cement rocket nozzle liner from the liquid-fueled rocket launched by Robert H. Goddard, likely the world's first on March 16, 1926. The piece measures approximately 1.25 x 2.25 x .5 inches and has scorch marks on the interior from use. This artifact was given to Frederick C. Durant III by Goddard’s widow, Esther Goddard, and has been kept in an envelope labeled in Durant’s hand, “Ceramic rocket nozzle liner used by R. H. Goddard in 1920s, possibly from the 1926 (March 16) flight.” Frederick C. Durant III, the former head of astronautics at the Smithsonian’s National Air and Space Museum, was one of the world’s foremost authorities of spaceflight and rocketry. This is one of several artifacts he received from Esther Goddard, one of the four people on the crew for the launch of March 16, 1926, and from her testimony, he determined the 1926 flight as the likely origin. The small size of the piece lends credence to this conclusion, as Goddard’s rocket experiments grew larger and larger over time. 2) Fuel valve remains from a failed experiment Bottom left. Fuel-feed-rate needle valve from one of Goddard’s early rockets, circa late 1920s/early 1930s. The piece measures approximately 7 x 5 x 2” and consists of a valve passing through a longer pipe segment attached to a fragment of a larger base; a short bracket extends from the base, which was damaged in a blast during rocket experiments. The needle valves were located near the top of Goddard’s rockets and were a critical element in controlling his fuel feed line and tank systems. This artifact was given to Frederick C. Durant III by Goddard’s widow, Esther Goddard. 3) Fuel Tank Baffle Upper left. Bi-level metal rocket fuel tank baffle from one of Goddard’s early rockets, circa mid-to-late 1920s. The piece measures approximately 3.5″ in diameter and 2.25″ tall and consists of two discs connected by four rods. This artifact was also given to Frederick C. Durant III by Goddard’s widow, Esther Goddard. The baffle was an important element of Goddard’s fuel tank design, used to combat the ‘slosh’ of liquid propellant during flight. A couple more Goddard quotes that remind me of @ElonMusk: “Every vision is a joke until the first man accomplishes it; once realized, it becomes commonplace.” "It is difficult to say what is impossible, for the dream of yesterday is the hope of today and the reality of tomorrow." — http://nitter.perennialte.ch/FutureJurvetson/status/2033606856325927058#m

Three weeks into the war with Iran, a number of observations as someone who spent years war-gaming this scenario. 1. The U.S. and Israel may have produced regime transition in the worst possible way. Ali Khamenei was 86 and had survived multiple bouts of prostate cancer. His death in the coming years would likely have triggered a real internal reckoning in Iran, potentially opening the door to somewhat more pragmatic leadership, especially after the protests and crackdown last month. Instead, the regime made its most consequential decision under existential external threat giving the hardliners a clear upperhand. Now we appear to have a successor who is 30 years younger, deeply tied to the IRGC, and radicalized by the war itself – including the killing of family members. Disastrous. 2. About seven years ago at CNAS, I helped convene a group of security, energy, and economic experts to walk through scenarios for a U.S.--Iran war and the implications for global oil prices. What we’re seeing now was considered one of the least likely but worst outcomes. The modeling assumed the Strait of Hormuz could close for 4–10 weeks, with 1–3 years required to restore oil production once you factored in infrastructure damage. Prices could spike from around $65 to $175–$200 per barrel, before eventually settling in the $80–$100 range a year later in a new normal. 3. One surprising development: Iran is still moving oil through the Strait of Hormuz while disrupting everyone else. In most war games I participated in, we assumed Iran couldn’t close the Strait and still use it themselves. That would have made the move extremely self-defeating. But Iran appears capable of harassing global shipping while still pushing some of its own exports through. That changes the calculus. 4. The U.S. now finds itself in the naval and air equivalent of the dynamic we faced in Iraq and Afghanistan. It’s a recipe for a quagmire where we win every battle and lose the war. We have overwhelming military dominance and are exacting a tremendous cost. But Iran doesn’t need to win battles. They just need occasional successes. A small boat hitting a tanker. A drone slipping through defenses in the Gulf. A strike on a hotel or oil facility. Each incident creates insecurity and drives costs up while remind everyone that the regime is surviving and fighting. 5. The deeper problem is that U.S. objectives were set far too high. Once “regime change” becomes the implicit or explicit goal, the bar for American success becomes enormous. Iran’s bar is simple: survive and keep causing disruption. 6. The options for ending this war now are all bad. You can try to secure the entire Gulf and Middle East indefinitely – extremely expensive and maybe impossible. You can invade Iran and replace the regime, but nobody is seriously going to do that. Costs are astronomical. You can try to destabilize the regime by supporting separatist groups. It probably won’t work and if it does you’ll most likely spark a civil war producing years of bloody chaos the U.S. will get blamed for. None of these are good outcomes. 7. The other escalatory options being discussed are taking the nuclear material out of Esfahan or taking Kargh Island. Esfahan is not really workable. Huge risk. You’d have been on the ground for a LONG time to safely dig in and get the nuclear material out in the middle of the country giving Iran time to reinforce from all over and over run the American position. 8. Kharg Island can be appealing to Trump. He’d love to take Iran’s ability to export oil off the map and try to coerce them to end the war. It’s much easier because it’s not in the middle of IRan. But it’s still a potentially costly ground operation. And again. Again, the Iranian government only has to survive to win and they can probably do that even without Kargh. 9. The least bad option is the classic diplomatic off-ramp. The U.S. declares that Iran’s military capabilities have been significantly degraded, which is how the Pentagon always saw the purpose of the war. Iran declares victory for surviving and demonstrating it can still threaten regional actors. It would feel unsatisfying. But this is the inevitable outcome anyway. Better to stop now than after five or ten more years of escalating costs. Remember in Afghanistan we turned down a deal very early in the war with the Taliban that looked amazing 20 years later. Don’t need to repeat that kind of mistake. 10. The U.S. and Israel are not perfectly aligned here. Trump just needs a limited win and would see long-term instability as a negative whereas for Netanyahu a weak unstable Iran that bogs the U.S. down in the MIddle East is a fine outcome. If President Trump decided he wanted Israel to stop, he likely has the leverage to push it in that direction just as he pressured Netanyahu to take a deal last fall on Gaza. 11. When this is over, the Gulf states will have to rethink their entire security strategy. They are stuck in the absolute worst place. They didn’t start this war and didn’t want it and now they are taking with some of the worst consequences. Neither doubling down with the U.S. and Israel nor placating the Iranians seems overwhelmingly appealing. 12. One clear geopolitical winner so far: Russia. Oil prices are rising. Sanctions are coming off. Western attention and military resources are shifting away from Ukraine. From Moscow’s perspective, this war is a win win win. 13. At some point China may have a role to play here. It is the world’s largest oil importer, and much of that supply comes from the Middle East. Yes they are still getting oil from Iran. But they also buy from the rest of the Middle East, and a prolonged disruption in the Gulf hits Beijing hard. That gives China a real incentive to help push toward an end to the conflict.

هشدار مشاور ترمپ درباره جنگ ایران: اسرائیل ممکن است به گزینه هسته‌ای روی آورد دیوید ساکس، مشاور امور هوش مصنوعی و ارز دیجیتال در دولت دونالد ترمپ، نسبت به ادامه جنگ میان امریکا، اسرائیل و ایران هشدار داده و گفته است که تشدید درگیری می‌تواند پیامدهای بسیار خطرناکی برای منطقه داشته باشد. او در اظهاراتی گفته است اگر جنگ برای هفته‌ها یا ماه‌ها ادامه پیدا کند، احتمال دارد اسرائیل با آسیب‌های جدی روبه‌رو شود و درگیری به مرحله‌ای برسد که کنترل آن دشوار باشد. ساکس هشدار داده است که در صورت ادامه جنگ، خطر تشدید بیشتر تنش‌ها وجود دارد. به گفته او، اگر فشارهای نظامی افزایش یابد و اسرائیل با تهدیدهای جدی روبه‌رو شود، ممکن است سناریوهایی مطرح شود که در آن حتی گزینه استفاده از سلاح هسته‌ای مورد بررسی قرار گیرد؛ موضوعی که به گفته او می‌تواند پیامدهای «فاجعه‌بار» برای منطقه و جهان داشته باشد. ساکس همچنین از دونالد ترمپ خواسته است که راهی برای پایان دادن سریع به جنگ پیدا کند. او گفته است که اکنون زمان آن است که امریکا به دنبال یک «راه خروج» از درگیری باشد و با استفاده از گزینه‌های سیاسی و دیپلماتیک، زمینه کاهش تنش‌ها و پایان جنگ با ایران را فراهم کند. به گفته او، یافتن چنین راهی می‌تواند از گسترش بیشتر بحران جلوگیری کند. ساکس تأکید کرده است که ادامه جنگ بدون چشم‌انداز روشن برای پایان آن، خطر تشدید درگیری و ورود منطقه به مرحله‌ای بسیار خطرناک‌تر را افزایش می‌دهد.

Today marks the birthday of Albert Einstein, one of the most famous scientists in history. One cannot easily overemphasize the mark his famous equation (E = mc^2) left not just on nuclear physics, but in many other areas of scientific innovation. A @NobelPrize Laureate and @TIME's Person of the Century, Einstein exhibited throughout his life a nearly unparalleled depth of knowledge and insight into science. Among others, he explained the relationship between mass and energy, which became part of the most famous equation in the world: E=mc^2. Einstein’s work on atomic energy is embodied in the IAEA’s work today: he is often credited as being the first to recognize that atomic energy could indeed be unlocked, laying the foundation for modern nuclear science. His keen awareness of the atom’s power also led him to strongly advocate for atomic energy to only be used for peaceful purposes. The legacy of this remarkable scientist lives on as we pursue our mission at the IAEA to enlarge the contribution of atomic energy to peace, health and prosperity throughout the world.

🔎Analyse de crédibilité : rumeurs sur la vie privée de Mojtaba Khamenei dans le contexte de la guerre informationnelle L’information trouve sa source primaire dans un article exclusif du New York Post publié le 16 mars 2026, relayé par une cascade de médias secondaires (WION, IranWire, IBTimes, OneIndia, etc.), et repose sur les déclarations de trois sources : deux officiels du renseignement américain et une troisième personne proche de la Maison Blanche, toutes affirmant que les agences d’espionnage américaines considèrent l’allégation comme crédible et non comme une opération de désinformation visant à fragiliser Mojtaba Khamenei. Le contenu central de l’allégation est le suivant : Mojtaba Khamenei aurait entretenu une relation sexuelle durable avec un homme qui fut son précepteur durant l’enfance , tandis qu’une troisième source diverge légèrement en indiquant que la personne concernée aurait plutôt été un employé de la famille Khamenei occupant une autre fonction, cette discordance entre sources affaiblissant la cohérence du récit. S’y ajoute l’allégation, non corroborée, selon laquelle Mojtaba Khamenei, blessé lors des frappes du 28 février qui ont tué son père, aurait, sous l’influence probable de puissants médicaments, effectué des avances sexuelles agressives envers ses soignants masculins. Sur le plan des éléments corroborants périphériques, un câble diplomatique américain de 2008, publié par WikiLeaks, mentionnait que Mojtaba avait épousé relativement tard, vers 30 ans, en raison d’un problème d’impuissance traité lors de plusieurs séjours prolongés dans des hôpitaux londoniens (Wellington et Cromwell), et qu’une quatrième visite de deux mois en Grande-Bretagne avait finalement été nécessaire avant que son épouse tombe enceinte, ce document évoque des problèmes médicaux mais ne mentionne en aucun cas l’orientation sexuelle, et sa réutilisation dans ce contexte relève d’une extrapolation. CBS News avait par ailleurs rapporté, sans préciser davantage, que le défunt ayatollah Ali Khamenei avait préféré un autre successeur en raison de certains « problèmes » non spécifiés dans la « vie personnelle » de son fils , ce qui constitue une convergence contextuelle notable mais non probante. La rumeur circulait déjà dans les cercles iraniens : son père et d’autres auraient soupçonné son homosexualité, et cette information aurait été propagée pour tenter de bloquer son accession au pouvoir , ce qui introduit un doute sérieux sur la motivation politique de la fuite. Sur le plan des limites majeures, les agences américaines ne disposent d’aucune preuve photographique ou vidéo, et aucun nom n’a été fourni ; la Maison Blanche n’a émis aucun commentaire officiel, aucune grande agence internationale indépendante (Reuters, AP, AFP) n’a confirmé l’information, et des responsables américains ont tenté de contenir la diffusion de cette information. Par ailleurs, le contexte géopolitique est lourdement chargé : les États-Unis sont en guerre ouverte avec l’Iran depuis les frappes de l’opération Epic Fury, Trump qualifie ouvertement Mojtaba de « lightweight » et d’« inacceptable », et la publication dans le New York Post, media à forte coloration éditoriale pro-Trump, via des sources anonymes au sein d’une administration engagée dans un conflit armé contre l’Iran constitue un facteur de décrédibilisation structurel majeur. En synthèse, la probabilité de véracité est à évaluer comme faible à modérée (30–40 %) : l’allégation peut être fondée sur un fragment de renseignement réel, mais elle est amplifiée, instrumentalisée et diffusée dans un cadre de guerre informationnelle manifeste, sans preuve matérielle vérifiable, avec des sources anonymes divergentes et une motivation politique évidente côté américain, ce qui en fait un élément à traiter avec une extrême prudence analytique.

I've seen several claims over the past two weeks that the United States "needs" Israel is because it provides the US with critically-needed intelligence. This is incorrect. It also ignores Israeli espionage inside the United States. A brief overview of both: First, the intelligence Israel provides Washington pertains to actors and conflicts only relevant to the United States because of the special relationship. The intelligence provided is on Israel’s adversaries. If Israel perceives them as threatening, it behooves Israel to provide the United States with this intelligence—they do not need American political, economic, or security incentives to do so. Moreover, this intelligence is often alarmist and politically motivated to push the United States toward confronting Israel’s enemies. Washington maintains a global intelligence apparatus more than capable of surveilling America’s adversaries without Israel. Second, there is a long history of Israeli espionage both inside the United States and targeting Americans abroad. The US intelligence community has highlighted this threat for decades—a leaked CIA document from 1979 discussing Israel’s foreign intelligence operations noted the United States is at the top of Israeli intelligence priorities, while US intel officials testifying to Congress in 2014 described Israel’s espionage activities in America as “unrivaled.” Israel and the lobby also go to great lengths to work around the Foreign Agents Registration Act (FARA) in their attempt to influence Washington. So long as Israel feels like it can continue such behavior without repurcussions, why would it ever stop? Industrial arable farming loses approximately 30 billion tonnes of topsoil per year globally. At current rates, we have about 60 harvests left before the soil that grows the world's crops is functionally depleted. Sixty harvests. About sixty years. Managed rotational cattle grazing builds topsoil at 1-2 inches per decade. Root systems deepen under grazing pressure. Manure feeds the soil biology. Hoof action increases water infiltration. Carbon moves from the atmosphere into the ground. This is how the North American Great Plains built six to eight feet of topsoil over millennia. Bison. Moving constantly. Never overgrazing any one area. The land thrived. Then we shot the bison, ploughed the grassland, planted continuous corn, and turned Kansas into a dust bowl within fifty years. The solution to topsoil loss is not fewer cattle. The solution to topsoil loss is more cattle, managed better, on more land. But that would require updating the narrative. The clock is ticking at thirty billion tonnes a year, and the narrative remains the priority.

Chris Van Hollen took aim at Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney, saying Carney warned about Trump’s assault on the international order at Davos, then “immediately signs up in support of the war in Iran.” He said that unless countries push back and demand accountability for civilian deaths in places like Gaza and the West Bank, and for unlawful wars like Iran, the world risks sliding into a system with no enforceable rules. Video Drop Site (@DropSiteNews) 🇨🇦 Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney told the World Economic Forum at Davos that the U.S.-led “rules-based international order” is finished and “will not return.” “For decades, countries like Canada benefited from what was called the rules-based international order,” Carney said. “We joined its institutions. We praised its principles. We benefited from its predictability.” But, he added, “we knew the story… was partially false.” “The strongest would exempt themselves when convenient,” Carney said, arguing that “trade rules were enforced asymmetrically,” and “international law applied with varying rigor depending on the identity of the accused or its victim.” “We participated in the rituals. And we largely avoided calling out the gaps between rhetoric and reality.” That “pleasant fiction,” he states, no longer works. The new world is one where economic integration and financial infrastructure are openly used by hegemons—hinting at the United States—as “weapons” for “economic coercion.” Carney rejected reliance on bilateral deals with dominant powers. “When we only negotiate bilaterally with a hegemon, we negotiate from weakness,” he said. “This is not sovereignty. It is the performance of sovereignty while accepting subordination.” Instead, he called for “values-based realism,” urging middle powers to act together and build a third path that is not a “world of fortresses,” but partnerships with partners with shared standards. If you are not at the table,” Carney said, “you are on the menu.” His remarks were met with a rare standing ovation in the room. Full speech below. WHO condemns this tragic loss of life and emphasizes that health workers must always be protected. According to international humanitarian law, medical personnel and facilities should never be attacked or militarized. The intensification of conflict in Lebanon and the broader Middle East increases the likelihood of such tragedies. Urgent action is required to de-escalate the crisis and protect the health of people throughout the region.
